text:
sam.k: Heads-up — after last night's base-image + nvidia-container-toolkit rollout we have ~12% of GPU nodes failing container startup with missing libcuda/libnvidia-ml mounts. Seeing this mostly on ubuntu-22.04 nodes in us-west-2 and smaller N-series instances.

jess: ack. any common error logs?

sam.k: logs show runtime error: "could not load /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1: No such file or directory" and containerd complaining about mount propagation. snippet: 
```
containerd: failed to start task: mount callback: mkdir /run/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/moby/...: no such file or directory
stderr: could not load libnvidia-ml.so: /host/usr/lib/...: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

infra-oncall: We're seeing node-level kubelet events: FailedMount for /usr/lib/nvidia -> host bind. Looks like toolkit changed the default mount path and our init script symlink isn't being created.

deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-18T01:12:34Z triggered base-image:redwood-gpu-ubuntu22-2026-03-18 and toolkit v1.14.0.

rahul: Repro on a local repro cluster: upgrading toolkit to v1.14 replaced host mountpoint from /usr/lib/nvidia -> /usr/local/nvidia and containerd's default mountPropagation=Private prevents the host symlink from showing up inside the container. Docker used to mask this.

lisa: any quick mitigation? we lost ~40 GPU slots from the pool, impacting Dedicated customers.

sam.k: short: cordon affected nodes, set scheduling to drain gracefully, revert toolkit to v1.11.0 on a small canary, and backfill capacity from us-east-1 if needed.

infra-oncall: I'm pushing a DaemonSet that will create legacy symlinks inside host namespaces as a stopgap: runs as privileged and ensures /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so -> /usr/local/nvidia/lib/libcuda.so. But this is brittle and only temporary.

rahul: ack. also adding a containerd config tweak to set mount_propagation: "Bidirectional" for GPU workloads so host mountpoints propagate. Will test on one node.

lisa: we should consider customers on Dedicated — notifying success teams. Cost hit if we spin up cross-region replacements; estimate ~$6k/day if we keep extra replacement capacity for 72h.

sam.k: raising internal incident INC-2026-215 and linking to infra ticket INFRA-9456. Plan: 1) patch canary with toolkit v1.11 + new kernel module symlink script; 2) if green, rollout; 3) if not, rollback base-image to previous AMI.

infra-oncall: Observability note: added alert for "nvidia mount failures" to the SRE dashboard with 5-min burn rate threshold.

ops-bot: Note: automated tester failed 6/6 GPU infra smoke tests after toolkit bump: https://ci.internal.redwood/test-runs/22345

jess: Action items: sam to coordinate canary rollback, rahul to test containerd mountPropagation change, infra-oncall to apply DaemonSet stopgap, lisa to notify CS & sales about capacity impact.

sam.k: I'll start the canary rollback now and update this thread with timestamps. If anyone sees new failures mention @infra-oncall and add logs to INFRA-9456. :facepalm:

infra-oncall: Canary started at 1783456900, toolkit v1.11 deployed to 3 nodes. Monitoring pods restarting...

sam.k: 1783457005 — canary looks healthy, libcuda visible, workloads scheduling. Will schedule rolling revert for remaining affected nodes in 15m window.

lisa: thanks team. Follow-up: add e2e gating for nvidia-container-toolkit changes in our AMI build pipeline and a unit test that validates host->container symlink visibility on containerd.

rahul: also logging note: create a parser to detect "libnvidia" mount errors in logs and auto-cordon node when threshold crossed to avoid scheduling to broken hosts.

jess: documented runbook update here: https://wiki.redwood/internal/runbooks/gpu-toolkit-mounts (draft)

sam.k: closing loop: rolling revert started 1783457050, will post final metrics after last node moves. Thanks all.
